label: CI runs
description: Pipeline runs with a decided outcome
explanation: Every CI pipeline run with a decided outcome, dated by the day the run started, whatever its trigger. Runs still in progress are not counted until they decide. History accumulates from when collection started; the source API retains only a bounded window, so earlier runs were never observable.

label: Gate pass rate
description: Share of commit-triggered runs that passed
explanation: Success share of gate runs — runs triggered by a push, a pull request, or the merge queue that reached a decided outcome (success, failure, or timeout). Cancelled and skipped runs decide nothing and stay out of both sides; runs waiting for a manual approval never executed and stay out as well.

label: First-try pass rate
description: Share of gate runs green without a retry
explanation: Gate runs that passed on their first attempt, as a share of all gate runs. The gap to the plain pass rate is the retry tax — green that had to be bought with a re-run.

label: Retried gate runs
description: Share of gate runs that were re-run
explanation: Gate runs whose final state came from a re-run, as a share of all gate runs. A retried run counts once, at its last attempt.

label: Gate run duration
description: Typical minutes a gate run takes
explanation: Median wall-clock minutes from a gate run's start to its decision, over decided runs dated by the day they started. Wall clock, not billable compute. Instant failures that never really ran are excluded from durations while still counting toward rates.

label: Gate run duration p90
description: Minutes the slowest tenth of gate runs exceed
explanation: The 90th percentile of gate run duration — nine in ten runs finish faster. The gap to the median is the bad-day penalty a developer actually waits for.

label: Gate run duration spread
description: How unevenly gate run durations vary
explanation: Sample standard deviation of gate run durations, in minutes. A pipeline whose duration swings wildly is harder to plan around than a slow but steady one.

label: CI hours
description: Wall-clock hours spent running CI
explanation: Wall-clock hours all decided runs spent executing, whatever the trigger. Not billable compute minutes — parallel jobs inside one run count as the run's elapsed time, not their sum. Filter by outcome to see hours burned on red runs.

label: Runs matching a collected commit
description: Decided runs whose head commit was collected
explanation: Decided runs whose head commit exists among the collected git commits. PR runs build synthetic merge refs and fork commits the commit stream never sees, so the gap between this and total runs is the honest ceiling for ANY analysis that joins CI to git history — chart it next to runs and collected commits to see how far the two streams can be trusted to join.

label: Commits collected
description: Git commits collected, by commit date
explanation: Commits the git connector collected, dated at their commit time — the other side of the run-to-commit join. Where runs far outnumber matched runs while commits stay high, CI is running on refs the commit stream does not see (PR merge refs, forks), not on missing history.

label: Deployments
description: Deployments created, by outcome
explanation: Deployments recorded in the period. The outcome is the latest status the deployment reached; one with no status yet shows as pending rather than being rounded away.

label: AI-added lines
description: Accepted added coding output
explanation: Accepted AI-generated added lines across coding AI tools.

label: AI-removed lines
description: Accepted deleted coding output
explanation: Accepted AI-generated removed lines across coding AI tools.

label: AI active days
description: Days with any AI activity across dev and assistant tools
explanation: Distinct days with person-attributed AI activity across dev and assistant tools.

label: AI potential cost
description: Potential cost of all AI usage at vendor rates, never the actual invoice
explanation: Person-attributed AI usage priced at the vendor's token rates — what the consumption would cost if billed purely by usage. It includes usage a seat already covered and excludes seat fees, so it is not the invoiced amount, and only tools that price usage per person contribute. Never add it to actual usage cost, which is the billed part of this same consumption.

label: AI seat cost
description: What a seat costs before any usage
explanation: The invoiced price of one seat for a billing month, from the invoice's per-seat amount. Dated at that month's first day, so a window must hold it to return the fee. The month comes from the read, not from the vendor. A seat whose tier the invoice does not price returns no value.

label: AI extra cost
description: Monthly cost billed on top of the seat fee, as last read
explanation: What the vendor billed on top of the seat fee, once included usage ran out. Exact as of that month's last reading, dated at its first day, so a window missing that day returns nothing — read the per-day distribution. The month comes from the read, not the vendor. Never added to potential usage cost.

label: AI extra cost, spread by day
description: The monthly billed cost spread across its days
explanation: The billed extra-usage cost placed on the days spent. Only a month-to-date total is reported, so a day is the step between readings — exact in sum against it, approximate in placement. The month comes from the read, so the 1st can cover several days. No reading means no point, and none is negative.

label: Extra-usage ceiling used
description: Share of the extra-usage ceiling consumed
explanation: Extra usage measured against the seat's ceiling. At 100% the vendor stops the seat, so this reads as proximity to being blocked, not waste. A seat with no ceiling returns no value, not zero. Above 100%, the ceiling was lowered below what the seat had spent. Its month comes from the read, not the vendor.

label: Accepted AI edits
description: Accepted tool or edit suggestions
explanation: Accepted AI edit or tool suggestions across supported coding AI tools.

label: AI tool acceptance
description: Accepted divided by offered AI edits
explanation: Accepted AI edit or tool suggestions divided by offered suggestions.

label: AI assistant messages
description: Assistant messages
explanation: Person-attributed assistant messages from supported AI assistant tools.

label: AI assistant actions
description: Assistant actions
explanation: Person-attributed assistant actions from supported AI assistant tools.

label: AI dev conversations
description: Coding tool conversations where the source reports them
explanation: Person-attributed conversations with coding AI tools, counted as the vendor counts them. For the agent tools this is the session or thread count — a session is the unit of conversation there, and no vendor publishes a separate conversation counter — so the number reads as "times the person started working with the assistant", not as messages exchanged. Tools that report no such unit, inline-completion tools among them, return no value rather than a zero.

label: AI chat conversations
description: Chat assistant conversations
explanation: Person-attributed chat assistant conversations from supported AI chat tools.

label: PRs with AI assistance
description: Pull requests the coding assistant touched
explanation: Pull requests where the coding assistant was active at least once, as the vendor attributes them. Reported only by sources that connect to the code host themselves, so a person working without that connection returns no value rather than a zero. Counts pull requests, not commits or lines, and says nothing about how much of the change the assistant wrote.

label: PRs seen by the AI vendor
description: Pull requests the AI vendor counted in the same window
explanation: Pull requests the AI vendor observed for the person, served as the context for PRs with AI assistance rather than as a goal of its own. It is the vendor's count over the vendor's own window, which need not be the day it is reported against and need not agree with the git sources — read it next to that measure, not next to git pull-request metrics.

label: Commits, any branch
description: Authored commits on any branch
explanation: Distinct authored commits on any branch across connected git sources, excluding merge commits.

label: Commits
description: Authored commits that reached the default branch
explanation: Authored commits reachable from the repository's default branch, or carried onto it by a merged pull request. A commit joins this metric when its branch lands, so a past period's figure rises as work merges. Dated by the commit, so the request that merged it can fall in a later period. Merge commits excluded.

label: Commits, other branches
description: Authored commits that have not reached the default branch
explanation: Authored commits not reachable from the repository's default branch — work in flight, or abandoned. A commit leaves this metric when its branch lands, so a past period's figure falls as work merges. Dated by the commit, not by the merge. A source reporting no branch membership counts here. Merge commits excluded.

label: Code lines, any branch
description: Lines added to code files on any branch
explanation: Lines added to files classified as code — tests, configuration, and documentation excluded. A commit whose diff was never collected has no classification, so its commit-level size stays out. Each change counts once: when the same change content appears in more than one commit, the lines belong to the first such commit.

label: Code lines
description: Lines added to code files that reached the default branch
explanation: Code lines whose commit is reachable from the repository's default branch, or was carried onto it by a merged pull request. Lines follow their commit, so this rises as work merges. Dated by the commit, not by the merge. Tests, configuration and documentation excluded.

label: Code lines, other branches
description: Lines added to code files that have not reached the default branch
explanation: Code lines whose commit has not reached the repository's default branch — work in flight, or abandoned. Lines follow their commit, so this falls as work merges. Dated by the commit, not by the merge. Tests, configuration and documentation excluded.

label: Lines added, any branch
description: All lines added on any branch, by file category
explanation: Lines added, attributed by file category when file changes are available; a commit whose diff was never collected contributes its commit-level size as Unknown. Each change counts once: when the same change content appears in more than one commit, the lines belong to the first such commit.

label: Lines added
description: All lines added that reached the default branch
explanation: Lines added whose commit is reachable from the repository's default branch, or was carried onto it by a merged pull request. Lines follow their commit, so this rises as work merges. Dated by the commit, not by the merge.

label: Lines added, other branches
description: All lines added that have not reached the default branch
explanation: Lines added whose commit has not reached the repository's default branch — work in flight, or abandoned. Lines follow their commit, so this falls as work merges. Dated by the commit, not by the merge.

label: Test change share
description: Share of implementation and test additions made in test files
explanation: Lines added to test files divided by lines added to code and test files. Documentation, configuration, and generated files do not affect the percentage. A result near zero can identify changes where tests are not evolving with implementation, but expected levels vary by repository and change type.

label: Lines removed, any branch
description: All lines removed on any branch, by file category
explanation: Lines removed, attributed by file category when file changes are available; a commit whose diff was never collected contributes its commit-level size as Unknown. Each change counts once: when the same change content appears in more than one commit, the lines belong to the first such commit.

label: Lines removed
description: All lines removed that reached the default branch
explanation: Lines removed whose commit is reachable from the repository's default branch, or was carried onto it by a merged pull request. Lines follow their commit, so this rises as work merges. Dated by the commit, not by the merge.

label: Lines removed, other branches
description: All lines removed that have not reached the default branch
explanation: Lines removed whose commit has not reached the repository's default branch — work in flight, or abandoned. Lines follow their commit, so this falls as work merges. Dated by the commit, not by the merge.

label: PRs opened, any branch
description: Authored pull requests into any branch
explanation: Pull requests opened into any branch, dated by creation.

label: PRs opened
description: Authored pull requests targeting the default branch
explanation: Pull requests opened against the repository's default branch, dated by creation. Unlike the commit and line splits this one is settled when the request is opened and does not move afterwards.

label: PRs opened, other branches
description: Authored pull requests targeting a branch other than the default
explanation: Pull requests opened against something other than the repository's default branch — a release branch, a stacked request, an integration branch. Dated by creation. A request whose destination the source does not report counts here rather than inventing an answer.

label: PRs merged, any branch
description: Authored pull requests merged into any branch
explanation: Authored pull requests that merged, dated by the merge in UTC — so a request counts in the period it landed and can carry commits written in earlier ones. Under a branch-scope breakdown the split says where the request was aimed, not where its commits sit.

label: PRs merged
description: Authored pull requests merged into the default branch
explanation: Pull requests that merged into the repository's default branch, dated by the merge. This is the surface that also promotes a branch's commits and lines into their default-branch metrics. A request counts in the period it merged, so it can carry commits written in earlier ones.

label: PRs merged, other branches
description: Authored pull requests merged into a branch other than the default
explanation: Pull requests that merged into something other than the repository's default branch, dated by the merge. Their commits do not count as having reached the default branch on this evidence alone. A request counts in the period it merged, so it can carry commits written in earlier ones.

label: PR merge rate, any branch
description: Share of pull requests created into any branch that merged
explanation: Of the pull requests created into any branch in the period, the share that have merged. Requests opened near the end of the period may not have merged yet, which lowers the rate at period edges.

label: PR merge rate
description: Share of pull requests created into the default branch that merged
explanation: Of the pull requests created into the default branch in the period, the share that have merged. Requests opened near the end of the period may not have merged yet, which lowers the rate at period edges.

label: PR abandonment rate
description: Share of created pull requests closed without merging
explanation: Of pull requests created in the period, the share now closed without merging. Open requests are not abandoned. Requests created near the period end can still change outcome later.

label: Review coverage
description: Share of created pull requests with at least one acting reviewer
explanation: Of pull requests created in the period, the share with at least one submitted review or approval. Assigned reviewers who never act do not count. Some sources provide approvals without review timestamps.

label: Reviewers per PR
description: Average number of acting reviewers per created pull request
explanation: Distinct reviewers who submitted a review or approval, divided by pull requests created in the period. Pull requests without review contribute zero, so read this with review coverage to separate breadth from coverage.

label: Multi-reviewer rate
description: Share of reviewed pull requests with more than one acting reviewer
explanation: Of pull requests with at least one submitted review or approval, the share with two or more distinct acting reviewers. This measures review breadth without conflating it with unreviewed pull requests.

label: Merges without approval
description: Share of merged pull requests with no reported approval
explanation: Of pull requests merged in the period, the share with no approval reported by the connected source. This can reveal missing approval gates, but source configuration and incomplete review history can also affect it.

label: Active commit days, any branch
description: Distinct days with at least one authored commit on any branch
explanation: Distinct calendar days with authored, non-merge commits. Repository breakdowns count active days independently; the total still counts each calendar day once across repositories.

label: Active commit days
description: Distinct days with at least one authored commit that reached the default branch
explanation: Distinct calendar days with authored, non-merge commits that reached the default branch. A commit joins when its branch lands, so a past period's figure rises as work merges. Repository breakdowns count active days independently; the total still counts each calendar day once across repositories.

label: Commits per active day, any branch
description: Cadence of commits on any branch, on days with commits
explanation: Commits on any branch divided by the number of days with at least one commit.

label: Commits per active day
description: Commits that reached the default branch, per day with at least one
explanation: Commits that reached the default branch, divided by the number of days with at least one such commit. A commit joins when its branch lands, so a past period's figure rises as work merges.

label: Commit size
description: Typical diff size per commit
explanation: Median diff size of authored commits (lines added plus removed), counting only content a commit is the first to introduce — a commit that repeats content already in the repository has a size of zero. Smaller commits are easier to review.

label: PR size
description: Typical diff size per pull request
explanation: Median diff size of authored pull requests (lines added plus removed), dated by the day the request was OPENED in UTC and counted whatever state the request reached. Smaller requests are easier to review. A source that never reported line counts contributes no value; a request whose counts were reported as zero — a rename or a mode change — contributes a zero, which is an observed diff of no lines rather than an absence.

label: Commits per PR
description: Typical number of commits per merged pull request
explanation: Median count of commits linked to authored pull requests, over requests merged in the period. A merged request whose commits the source does not link contributes no value.

label: PR cycle time
description: Typical hours from open to merge
explanation: Median hours from opening a pull request to merging it, dated by the merge in UTC, over requests merged in the period. Mostly waiting — for a reviewer, for a build, for someone to press merge — so it describes the path a change travels rather than the person who opened it. A source that does not report a merge time contributes no duration.

label: PR cycle time (p75)
description: Slow-end hours from open to merge
explanation: 75th percentile of hours from opening a pull request to merging it, dated by the merge in UTC, over requests merged in the period. Reads the same waiting as the median and describes the same path, so it too is not a statement about the person who opened the request.

label: Time to first review
description: Typical hours from pull request creation to first review
explanation: Median hours from opening a pull request to its first submitted review, over first reviews recorded in the period. Pull requests without a review and sources without review timestamps contribute no duration.

label: Time to first review (p75)
description: Slow-end hours from pull request creation to first review
explanation: 75th percentile of hours from opening a pull request to its first submitted review, over first reviews recorded in the period. Pull requests without a review and sources without review timestamps contribute no duration.

label: Review wait share
description: Typical share of pull request cycle time spent waiting for first review
explanation: Median percentage of open-to-merge time elapsed before the first submitted review, over merged pull requests in the period. Sources without review timestamps contribute no value. High values suggest first review is the main cycle-time constraint.

label: Review-to-merge time
description: Typical hours from first review to merge
explanation: Median hours from first submitted review to merge, over merged pull requests in the period. Sources without review timestamps contribute no value. Read with time to first review to locate delay before or after review starts.

label: Approval-to-merge time
description: Typical hours from latest timestamped approval to merge
explanation: Median hours from the latest reported approval with a timestamp to merge, over merged pull requests in the period. Sources that expose approvals without per-approval timestamps contribute no value. High values can identify delay after review gates clear.

label: Reviews performed
description: Review verdicts submitted on pull requests
explanation: Review verdicts the person submitted on any pull request, dated by submission. This is the reviewer's side of review coverage — it counts the reviews a person performed, not the reviews their own requests received.

label: PR comments
description: Comments written on pull requests
explanation: Comments the person wrote on pull requests — conversation and inline review comments alike — dated by posting. The comment target dimension splits comments on the person's own requests from comments on other people's; a comment whose request author cannot be determined counts under others, so the two halves always add up to the total.

label: Chat messages sent
description: Chat messages sent
explanation: Chat messages a person sent across messaging tools. Counts are not directly comparable between tools: Slack includes thread replies, and Microsoft Teams combines private-chat and channel messages.

label: Channel messages
description: Messages posted to shared channels, including replies
explanation: Messages a person posted to shared channels, posts and thread replies together, across messaging tools. Tools that report posts and replies separately are folded so counts stay comparable.

label: Private chat share
description: Share of chat messages sent outside shared channels
explanation: Private-chat messages divided by all chat messages. Private chat is one-to-one and group chats in Microsoft Teams, and everything outside channels in Slack, so it is not limited to one-to-one conversations. Counted only in tools that tell private chat and channels apart; messages from tools without that split, such as Zulip, are left out, and a person with only those tools has no value. A lower share means more communication happens in open channels.

label: Chat messages per active day
description: Chat messages divided by chat-active days
explanation: Chat messages sent divided by the distinct days with chat messages in any tool, so a day spent in two tools counts once.

label: Active days
description: Days with collaboration activity
explanation: Distinct days on which a person took a deliberate collaboration action — sending a message, sending email, engaging or sharing a file, or attending a meeting or call. Passive activity such as receiving or reading email is excluded.

label: Emails sent
description: Emails sent
explanation: Emails a person sent. Replies and forwards count; a message to several recipients counts once.

label: Emails received
description: Emails received
explanation: Messages delivered to the mailbox, including mailing lists and automated notifications. Measures inbox volume, not work, and is not comparable with read events.

label: Email read events
description: Email read events
explanation: Counts every time a message is marked read, as Exchange reports it: reopening a message or marking a whole folder read counts each message again. Not the number of distinct emails read, so it can exceed emails received.

label: Files viewed or edited
description: Files viewed or edited
explanation: Files a person viewed, edited, uploaded or downloaded in OneDrive and SharePoint, counted once per file per day and summed over the period. A bulk upload or download counts every file, so one such day can outweigh weeks of ordinary work. Files the OneDrive sync client syncs are reported separately and do not count.

label: Files shared, internal
description: Files shared inside the organization
explanation: Files a person shared with people inside the organization, counted once per file per day and summed over the period, so a file shared on several days counts once for each of those days. A share with a group counts as inside even when the group has outside members.

label: Files shared, external
description: Files shared outside the organization
explanation: Files a person shared with people outside the organization, counted once per file per day and summed over the period, so a file shared on several days counts once for each of those days.

label: Files shared
description: Files shared with any recipient
explanation: Files a person shared with recipients inside or outside the organization, counted once per file per day in each scope and summed over the period, so a file shared on several days counts once for each of those days. A file shared both inside and outside on the same day counts twice, once in each scope, and a share with a group counts as inside even when the group has outside members.

label: Meeting hours
description: Hours in meetings and calls, estimated from daily totals
explanation: Hours spent in meetings and calls; Microsoft Teams includes one-to-one calls. Microsoft Teams reports audio, video and screen-share time only as daily totals, so a Teams day counts the longest of the three, an estimate rather than exact meeting time. Zoom time counts only while someone else was in the meeting, so a room left open or a pause with nobody else adds nothing.

label: Meetings
description: Distinct meetings and one-to-one calls attended
explanation: Distinct meetings a person attended across meeting tools. Microsoft Teams one-to-one calls count as meetings, as two-person Zoom meetings do. The kind breakdown tells Teams scheduled meetings, Teams ad hoc meetings (Meet Now from a chat) and Teams calls apart; Zoom reports no such split, so Zoom meetings are one kind.

label: Meeting-free days
description: Active days with no meeting or call time
explanation: Days on which a person was actively collaborating but spent no time in meetings or calls — a proxy for uninterrupted working days. Only addresses some meeting source reports on count, so a person no meeting tool knows has no value.

label: Time outside meetings
description: Share of the workday outside meetings and calls
explanation: Share of the workday not spent in meetings or calls, over the days a person was active: 100 minus meeting hours as a share of scheduled working hours. Meeting time counts up to the working hours of the day and address it was recorded under. Scheduled hours default to a nominal eight-hour day where an HR source does not provide them. Only addresses some meeting source reports on count, so a person no meeting tool knows has no value.

label: Meetings organized
description: Meetings organized
explanation: Meetings a person organized in Microsoft Teams or Zoom. A Zoom meeting counts for its host on the day it started, and only if someone besides the host attended.

label: Issues closed
description: Every issue closed in the tracker
explanation: All issues a person moved into a closed status during the period. Bugs are part of this number and are listed separately by type.

label: Bugs closed
description: Bug-type issues closed
explanation: Issues of a bug type a person closed during the period. Part of issues closed, not a separate total.

label: Tasks closed
description: Closed issues of a known task (non-bug) type
explanation: Issues of a known task (non-bug) type a person closed during the period. Issues whose type cannot be determined are excluded rather than counted here.

label: Unclassified issues closed
description: Closed issues whose type is not mapped to a kind by the operator table
explanation: Issues a person closed whose type the operator type table maps to no kind, so they count in neither bugs nor tasks. Completes the split of issues closed.

label: Closed fixed
description: Closed issues resolved as really done
explanation: Issues a person closed during the period whose resolution class is fixed — work that was really done rather than dismissed. Part of issues closed, not a separate total.

label: Closed duplicates
description: Closed issues resolved as duplicates
explanation: Issues a person closed during the period whose resolution class is duplicate. Part of issues closed, not a separate total.

label: Closed won't-fix
description: Closed issues resolved as won't-fix
explanation: Issues a person closed during the period whose resolution class is wontfix. Part of issues closed, not a separate total.

label: Time to resolution
description: Issue lifetime from creation to close
explanation: Median time from issue creation to close.

label: Pickup time
description: Wait before work starts on an issue
explanation: Median time from issue creation to first entering an in-progress status.

label: Flow efficiency
description: Active development share of issue lifetime
explanation: Time in active development as a share of total issue lifetime, across closed issues.

label: Reopen rate
description: Closed issues reopened shortly after
explanation: Share of issue closes followed by a reopen within 14 days.

label: Due date compliance
description: On-time share of issues with a due date
explanation: Share of issues that had a due date and were closed on or before it.

label: On-time delivery
description: On-time share of all closed issues
explanation: Share of all closed issues that were closed on or before their due date.

label: Average slip
description: How late overdue issues close
explanation: Average days past the due date for issues closed late.

label: Estimation accuracy
description: How close estimates land to time spent
explanation: 100 minus the average deviation between original estimates and time spent, over days whose estimated work stayed within twice the estimate. 100 means estimates matched reality; over- and under-estimation count equally.

label: Logged time
description: Hours logged against issues
explanation: All work time logged in the tracker during the period, whatever the issue's status on the day it was logged.

label: Worklog accuracy
description: Logged time versus tracked development
explanation: Logged work time as a share of time issues spent in in-progress statuses.

label: Bug share
description: Bugs as a share of all closed issues
explanation: Bug-type issues as a share of all closed issues, issues of an undetermined type included in the denominator. A share, so it cannot exceed 100%.

label: Stale in progress
description: Open issues idle for over two weeks
explanation: Open issues with no status change in more than 14 days.

label: Pages created
description: Wiki pages authored
explanation: Wiki pages the person created during the period, counted on the page's creation date.

label: Page edits
description: Wiki edit sessions
explanation: Logical wiki edits the person made during the period. Consecutive saves of the same page within a short window count as one edit, so autosaves do not inflate the number.

label: Pages edited
description: Distinct wiki pages edited
explanation: Distinct wiki pages the person edited during the period, counted per day the page was touched.

label: Comments received
description: Comments on the person's wiki pages
explanation: Comments and replies other people left on wiki pages the person authored — a signal of how much their documentation is read and discussed.
